subject: Model fit & token forecast for BrightHealth onboarding

Subject: Re: Quick context on model choices for our ingest pipeline

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We want to lock down the model/size guidance before our kickoff next Wednesday. A few specifics from our side: the clinical summarizer will ingest documents averaging 8,500 characters (~1,600 tokens), but we do expect some long documents up to ~25k chars (~4,800 tokens). Average daily volume is projected at ~12k requests/day, with a bursty peak to 1,200 concurrent requests during nightly processing windows.

Can you share an initial model shortlist and a rough token-cost forecast? Also tell us whether longer-context models are recommended or whether chunking + stitching would be better.

Appreciate any guidance (and examples of what you recommend for an initial canary).

— Alice
Alice Wu
Director, Integrations — BrightHealth
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Alice Wu <alice.wu@brighthealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick context on model choices for our ingest pipeline

Hi Alice — thanks for the details. Attaching a short worksheet (brighthealth_token_estimates_v1.xlsx) and a one-page shortlist (redwood_model_shortlist_notes.pdf) — see links below. High level guidance up front:

- Shortlist: 1) Llama2-70B-Chat (quantized variant) for high-quality single-turn summarization; 2) Mistral-Instruct-XXL for cost-forward workloads; 3) RedOpt-13B (our tuned/verified variant) as a cost-effective baseline.
- Context strategy: given your single-doc median ~1.6k tokens and occasional ~4.8k tokens, we recommend a hybrid approach: prefer full-context models for documents <= 4k tokens; use deterministic chunking (4k-window, 512-token overlap) + stitching for longer docs. This preserves coherence and keeps latency predictable.
- Throughput and concurrency: based on 12k/day (average) with 1,200 peak concurrent during batch windows, expect the following rough GPU footprints (initial canary):
  * Llama2-70B-q8: 4 dedicated A100s (or equivalent), autoscale to 6 during peak batch windows.
  * Mistral-XXL: 2-3 A100s with aggressive batching; recommended batching window 40–80ms in Dedicated.
  * RedOpt-13B-q4: 1 instance pool (4 GPUs) for steady traffic and lowest unit cost.

- Token cost estimate (very rough): assuming typical generation of 300 tokens per summary:
  * Llama2-70B-q8: ~0.009 USD per generated token-equivalent (hosted pricing varies) — monthly ~0.009 * 300 * 12k ≈ $32,400 (generation only) — see workbook for prompt+response breakdown.
  * Mistral-XXL: ~0.0035 per gen-token — monthly ≈ $12,600.
  * RedOpt-13B-q4: ~0.0022 per gen-token — monthly ≈ $7,920.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical sizing call with Dev and your infra lead to validate concurrency and batching assumptions (I can coordinate this week).
2) Canary plan: start with RedOpt-13B (1-week trial, 10% traffic, end-to-end telemetry) then expand to Mistral if quality trade-offs are acceptable. Reserve Llama2-70B for higher-quality slices where cost is less sensitive.

I've included a short appendix in the PDF with configuration hints (context windows, recommended quantization level, batching policy). If helpful, we can run a small sample pass on 20 documents to produce actual latency & token counts.

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: brighthealth_token_estimates_v1.xlsx; redwood_model_shortlist_notes.pdf

Alice — quick technical follow-up from my side (Dev, infra at Redwood). Re: chunking & stitching:

- For docs >4k tokens we recommend deterministic chunking with overlap and a single stitching call that passes the chunk outputs into a focused summarizer prompt. This gives better coherence and avoids context overflow.
- Latency targets: for nightly batch window (burst concurrency ~1,200) we assume lower SLO (500–1,200 ms per request depending on chosen model). If you need strict sub-200 ms tail latency we should plan a more aggressive dedicated pool and fewer context windows.
- KV-cache and prefix caching: enable prefix caching for repeated templates (billing headers, templated text) — this reduces token compute for partial repeats.
- Concrete numbers from local benchmarks (your average doc size ~1.6k tokens):
  * RedOpt-13B-q4: p95 latency ~220 ms on a 1-GPU instance with batching 64. (est. throughput ~1,500 req/min per 4-GPU pool)
  * Mistral-XXL: p95 ~360 ms with batching 96. (est. throughput ~2,000 req/min per 4-GPU pool)
  * Llama2-70B-q8: p95 ~620 ms; memory-limited, requires sharded alloc.

I'll prepare a short sizing diagram and a suggested Dedicated capacity commit for a two-month pilot (numbers in the workbook). Can we set the sizing call for Tue 30 Jun at 10:00 PT?

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
